screenSummary.playArea: The play area is a Hertzsprung–Russell diagram: temperature runs along the horizontal axis, hottest on the left, and luminosity up the vertical axis. A star marker sits on it, beside the Sun.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area has sliders for the star's temperature and luminosity, its radius and magnitude, checkboxes for guide lines, axis choices, and a size comparison with the Sun.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Move the star with the arrow keys or the sliders and watch its radius change.

explore.currentDetailsPattern: Your star has a temperature of {{temperature}} kelvin, a luminosity of {{luminosity}} times the Sun's and a radius of {{radius}} times the Sun's.

controls.cursorStarHelp: Left and right arrows change the temperature, up and down arrows the luminosity. Hold Shift for small steps.

screenSummary.playArea: The play area is an HR diagram with lines of equal radius and two stars, A and B, that you can move.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area compares the two stars' temperatures, luminosities and radii, shows them to scale, and lets you keep a star's luminosity or temperature fixed while it moves.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Keep the luminosity fixed and make star B hotter: watch its radius shrink.

radius.currentDetailsPattern: Star B is {{temperature}} times as hot as star A, {{luminosity}} times as luminous, and {{radius}} times as large.

controls.starHelp: Arrow keys move the star across the diagram. Hold Shift for small steps.

screenSummary.playArea: The play area is an HR diagram of real stars from the Gaia and Hipparcos catalogues: the stars nearest the Sun, the brightest stars in the sky, or both.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area chooses which stars to plot and which kinds of star to show, finds a star by name, and shows the selected star's properties. Under the diagram are guide lines and axis choices.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Compare the nearest stars with the brightest: are bright stars close, luminous, or both?

controls.starsHelp: Left and right arrows select the next cooler or hotter star.
controls.selectedPattern: {{name}}: {{temperature}} kelvin, {{luminosity}} times the Sun's luminosity, {{radius}} times its radius.

screenSummary.playArea: The play area is an HR diagram of about 44 000 real stars: a random one in ten of all the stars Gaia found within 100 parsecs of the Sun.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area sets a distance limit and an optional brightness limit, shows what share of the plotted stars are dwarfs, subgiants, giants, supergiants and white dwarfs, and colours the stars by kind or by distance. Under the diagram are guide lines and axis choices.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Turn on the brightness limit at V = 6: which kinds of star does the naked eye see, compared with all the stars nearby?

gaiaCensus.currentDetailsPattern: {{count}} stars are plotted: {{dwarfs}} percent main-sequence dwarfs, {{giants}} percent giants and subgiants, {{whiteDwarfs}} percent white dwarfs.
